Package hadur2.core.gun

Class GunController

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.gun.GunController
public class GunController extends Object
The duel's gun: owns every opponent's gun views, picks which gun aims, scores the virtual guns, learns from each gun wave as it breaks, and chooses the bullet power.

Where it sits in the tick: HadurCore builds a gun wave at every scan of the enemy and hands broken waves to onWaveBreak(hadur2.core.model.Wave, java.util.List<hadur2.core.model.RobotState>); on each duel tick it calls aim(hadur2.core.model.Wave, java.awt.geom.Point2D.Double, long) (once the gun is within three ticks of cooling) and, when a real bullet goes out, fireVirtualBullets(hadur2.core.model.Wave, java.awt.geom.Point2D.Double, long). It asks calculateBulletPower(double, double, double, int) for the power of the next wave, which the core's power policy may then raise (POW-1, POW-2 live there). The opening book's and the tick budget's decisions come in through setOpening(hadur2.core.gun.GunController.Opening) and setKShare(double), and the opponent profile's seeds through seed(java.lang.String, double[], hadur2.core.model.SeedWeight).

Which gun aims, in a duel:

  1. With an opening from the profile, that gun from the first wave (ADAPT-1), until the live virtual-gun ratings differ by more than their margin of error (DIAL-1, GUN-1).
  2. Otherwise head-on until the main view holds DATA_THRESHOLD points that still count, then whichever gun's live rating is highest by more than the margin of error (GUN-1's margin-gated form of 1.20's rule), main on a tie or while nothing clears it.

GUN-4's third gun (the hybrid gun, see HybridGun) joins that live comparison, in both cases, only while its gate is open: the live movement tier is M2 or M3, or the plain main-vs-anti-surfer verdict already favours a switch. It is always rated alongside the other two (see fireVirtualBullets(hadur2.core.model.Wave, java.awt.geom.Point2D.Double, long)), gate open or not, so it already has a history once the gate opens. Every live rating decays each shot with a 100-shot half-life (GUN-1), so a surfer that changes its movement mid-battle can flip the choice again.

GUN-5 splits all of that by the power class of the shot. Every real duel bullet rates the virtual guns, in the table of its own class: bullets under 0.2 (LIGHT_BELOW) in the light table, the rest in the other. The gun for a shot is read from the table of the class the shot's wave carries (the core decides the power before it aims), so light bullets, which are about nine shots in ten under the lead-aware rule, no longer share a verdict with the rare heavy ones. SampledGun is the light class's fourth candidate. A class with no verdict yet fires as the combined rule did with none: the opening gun, else the main gun. Ratings are not kept in the profile (see docs/requirements.md, D3 notes).

With several opponents at the battle's start only the main gun aims and no virtual guns are scored.

Growth is bounded (RES-2): views are per opponent name and each is capped by its tree; the virtual bullets are keyed by wave and cleared at each round's start. Angles are Robocode bearings in radians (0 north, clockwise); guess factors are in [-1, 1].

    • aim

      public double aim(Wave w, Point2D.Double myNextLocation, long currentTime, ShadowValue shadow)
      GUN-7: aim(Wave, Point2D.Double, long), then the shot's angle chosen among a few nearby candidates by the damage a hit would do plus the damage the bullet's shadows save us (ShadowAim). The chosen gun still decides which angle is the centre of the choice; the virtual guns are rated on their own angles, not on the shifted one.

      Without a shadow term, with SHADOW_AIM off, while no wave has a published interval, and in the head-on warm-up, the answer is the plain aim's, exactly.

      Parameters:
      w - the latest gun wave at the target
      myNextLocation - where we will be when the bullet leaves, the next tick
      currentTime - the present tick
      shadow - what a firing angle's shadows are worth, or null for none
      Returns:
      an absolute bearing in radians

    • margin

      static double margin(double hits, double n)
      The 95% margin of error of a rate of hits in n (Agresti-Coull).

      Agresti-Coull adds z^2 / 2 (about 2) successes and z^2 (about 4) trials, with z = 1.96, before taking the normal approximation's half-width z * sqrt(p (1 - p) / n). The adjustment keeps the margin sensible at small n and at rates near 0, where the plain formula gives a margin of zero.

    • fireVirtualBullets

      public void fireVirtualBullets(Wave w, Point2D.Double myNextLocation, long currentTime)
      Fires one virtual bullet for each of the three guns along with a real bullet: records the angle each gun would have fired on w, to be scored when the wave breaks. Duels only. The core skips this call at its lowest computation level (TIME-1, TIME-2).

      The hybrid gun is always rated here, whether or not GUN-4's gate is open, so it already has a history by the time the gate opens rather than starting from nothing.

      Parameters:
      w - the wave the real bullet rides
      myNextLocation - where we will be when the bullet leaves
      currentTime - the present tick

    • shieldAttackFired

      public void shieldAttackFired(Wave w, Point2D.Double myLocation, long currentTime, double firedPower, boolean virtualGuns)
      SHIELD-6, GUN-5: a real shield-mode attack shot went out at firedPower, which the shield may have cut from the wave's. The virtual guns are rated in the class of that power (unless the tick budget has shed them) and the sampled gun's phase moves on. An intercept bullet, shot at an enemy bullet, is no attack and does not come here.
      Parameters:
      w - the wave the real bullet rides
      myLocation - where the bullet leaves from
      currentTime - the present tick
      firedPower - the power the real bullet was fired at
      virtualGuns - whether the virtual guns are scored this tick (TIME-1, TIME-2)

    • virtualGunScores

      public double[] virtualGunScores(String botName)
      The virtual guns' battle totals against botName: main-gun waves, main weighted hits, anti-surfer waves, anti-surfer weighted hits. Zeros before any virtual bullet.

      These are the undecayed lifetime totals for the battle, not GUN-1's decayed live rating: what folds into the profile (MEM-2) must stay a plain count across the whole battle, since the profile is read across future battles too, where GUN-1's 100-shot half-life (meant to let this battle's live choice track a surfer that changes movement mid-fight) has no meaning. The core also checks the gun seed against the main gun's rating here (RES-4). The hybrid gun's rating is not folded into the profile (GUN-4 is a live, in-battle gate only; the profile format is unchanged).

      Parameters:
      botName - the opponent
      Returns:
      four totals, as above
